issue_paraphrase: An error object raised for invalid JSON cannot be serialized with pickle and then deserialized: round-tripping it through pickle (which is what happens when a process pool re-raises a worker exception) raises a TypeError complaining that two constructor arguments are missing, and even when it does come back the reconstructed object does not have the same repr. Any program that pickles this exception, for example multiprocessing pools whose workers fail on malformed JSON, crashes on the unpickle step.
fix_summary: Added an explicit __reduce__ to requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError that delegates to the json library's JSONDecodeError.__reduce__, because the multiple-inheritance MRO caused IOError's reduce (single msg arg) to be used and drop the doc/pos constructor arguments.
notes: Fully self-contained, no network, fast (<1s). Reproduction is a one-liner; the project's own pytest regression test also works with just 'pytest' installed (no pytest-httpbin needed). Environment for verification: bench-base:python-3.12 image, requests installed with editable install. Parent commit is from 2024; pyproject layout at that commit is compatible with the modern install recipe used here.

issue_paraphrase: When the environment's no_proxy list contains a hostname such as example.com, the library decides to bypass proxies for any host that merely ends with that string, so badexample.com (or prelocalhost against localhost) is also excluded from proxying even though it should not be. In the other direction, a dotted entry like .example.com no longer matches the exact bare host example.com. The proxy-bypass decision is wrong at domain boundaries in both ways.
fix_summary: Ported CPython bpo-39057 fix for the same bug in urllib.request: first try an exact hostname/port match, then compare endswith against the entry prefixed with a leading dot so only real subdomains match; entries with a leading dot are normalized by stripping it before the exact match.
notes: Fully self-contained, no network, runs in <1s. No dependency pins strictly required; the bug is pure code logic. Uses no pytest-httpbin; 'pytest' + requests editable install suffices for the golden test.

issue_paraphrase: A header whose name or value ends with a newline character is treated as valid: unlike newlines in the middle of a header, a trailing newline is silently accepted by the header-validity check, so a request header such as {'foo': 'bar\n'} proceeds without the invalid-header error that embedded return characters trigger. Header values consisting of only a newline are also accepted. Malformed trailing newlines should be rejected like any other return character.
fix_summary: Changed the header name/value validity regular expressions from anchoring with $ to \Z, because in Python's re module $ matches just before a trailing newline, which let header names/values ending with '\n' pass validation. \Z requires the true end of the string.

A Content-Type parameter without an equals sign (e.g. 'text/html; charset') was parsed as {key: True}, and reading the charset crashed instead of falling back to the text default. Buggy code confirmed present at parent: 'if param: key, value = param, True' plus 'value = param[index_of_equals + 1 :].strip(items_to_strip)' guarded by index_of_equals; _parse_content_type_header('text/html; charset') returns ('text/html', {'charset': True}). install_recipe: git config --global --add safe.directory /work/requests && cd /work/requests && git reset --hard <sha> && git clean -fd && python3 -m pip install -e '.[socks]' pytest
issue_paraphrase: A Content-Type header whose parameter lacks an equals sign, such as 'text/html; charset', makes charset/encoding parsing crash: the value-less parameter is stored as a boolean True, and when the charset is then read from the parsed parameters the code calls .strip() on the boolean and raises AttributeError instead of falling back to the default encoding for text content. Malformed valueless parameters should be ignored so the response encoding resolution degrades gracefully.
fix_summary: Rewrote _parse_content_type_header so that only parameters containing '=' are recorded; parameters without '=' are skipped instead of being stored with a True placeholder, preventing bool objects from reaching downstream .strip() calls.
notes: Fully offline and deterministic (<1s). Note the parent of this fix (bc7dd0fc) is itself the fix commit of the adjacent #7308 change; they are independent bugs in different files. No pytest-httpbin needed for reproduction or goldens. All three golden tests are plain parametrized tests without fixtures.

An object that forwards attribute lookups to an underlying binary stream but does not define __iter__ itself is not recognized as a stream, so request preparation tries to encode it as form parameters and crashes. At fix 6404f345: prepare() succeeds and the body stream is passed through untouched, and the golden test passes (response echoes 'data' after the 307 redirect). install_recipe: git config --global --add safe.directory /work/requests && cd /work/requests && git reset --hard <sha> && git clean -fd && python3 -m pip install -e '.[socks]' pytest
issue_paraphrase: Passing a file-like object as the request body data that does not define __iter__ itself but forwards attribute lookups to an underlying stream (a common wrapper pattern, e.g. objects produced by lazy file proxies) makes request preparation fail with a TypeError claiming the object is not iterable, even though it is a perfectly readable stream. The wrapper should be recognized as a streaming body and sent as-is, and it should survive a redirect re-post.
fix_summary: In PreparedRequest.prepare_body, replaced the isinstance(data, Iterable) check with an explicit hasattr(data, '__iter__') fallback so duck-typed stream wrappers whose __getattr__ proxies to the underlying file are detected as streams instead of being fed to form-encoding.
notes: Primary reproduction is fully offline (prepare() only; no sending) and fast. The upstream golden test posts through a local httpbin 307 redirect, which needs pytest-httpbin/httpbin and therefore flask/werkzeug wheels (flask is a Terminal-Bench 2.1 source repo - prefer the direct repro, or accept flask wheels in the image); no network needed either way. Related follow-up fixes exist for the same wrapper pattern in _encode_files (#7502) and remaining protocol isinstance checks (#7505).
